arxiv-2105-00422.title: Boundary quotient C*-algebras of semigroups Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 46L08, 46L05, 47L55, 20M32 Thanks: Key words and phrases: Semigroup algebras, partial crossed product, coactions, boundary quotient, C*-envelope.
arxiv-2105-00422.creator: Evgenios T.A. Kakariadis, Elias G. Katsoulis, Marcelo Laca, Xin Li
arxiv-2105-00422.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Evgenios T.A. Kakariadis, Elias G. Katsoulis, Marcelo Laca, Xin Li. We study two classes of operator algebras associated with a unital subsemigroup P P of a discrete group G G : one related to universal structures, and one related to co-universal structures. First we provide connections between universal C*-algebras that arise variously from isometric representations of P P that reflect the space 𝒥 \mathcal{J} of constructible right ideals, from associated Fell bundles, and from induced partial actions.

arxiv-2212-00120.title: The lstMCpipe library
arxiv-2212-00120.creator: Enrique García, Thomas Vuillaume, Lukas Nikel
arxiv-2212-00120.description: Abstract The Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA) is the next generation of ground-based gamma-ray astronomy observatory that will improve the sensitivity of current generation instruments by one order of magnitude. The LST-1 is the first telescope prototype built on-site on the Canary Island of La Palma and has been taking data for a few years already.

arxiv-2302-03682.title: Approximate message passing from random initialization with applications to ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} synchronization
arxiv-2302-03682.creator: Gen Li Wei Fan Yuting Wei
arxiv-2302-03682.description: Abstract This paper is concerned with the problem of reconstructing an unknown rank-one matrix with prior structural information from noisy observations. While computing the Bayes-optimal estimator seems intractable in general due to its nonconvex nature, Approximate Message Passing (AMP) emerges as an efficient first-order method to approximate the Bayes-optimal estimator.

arxiv-2305-03348.title: Flock: Accurate network fault localization at scale Conference: ; June 2023; To appear
arxiv-2305-03348.creator: Vipul Harsh, Tong Meng, Kapil Agrawal, P. Brighten Godfrey
arxiv-2305-03348.description: Abstract . Inferring the root cause of failures among thousands of components in a data center network is challenging, especially for “gray” failures that are not reported directly by switches. Faults can be localized through end-to-end measurements, but past localization schemes are either too slow for large-scale networks or sacrifice accuracy.

arxiv-2404-07401.title: On twisted Kawamata’s semi-positivity and finite generation of generalized canonical rings
arxiv-2404-07401.creator: Yoshinori Gongyo, Shigeharu Takayama
arxiv-2404-07401.description: Abstract . We give a twisted version of the Kawamata semi-positivity theorem by the ℚ \mathbb{Q} -line bundle with a vanishing Lelong number at every point. Moreover, we apply the result to the finite generation problem for canonical rings of Birkar’s generalized pairs. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 14D06, 14E30, 32J25 1.

arxiv-2601-12387.title: Microscopic origin of orbital magnetization in chiral superconductors
arxiv-2601-12387.creator: Jihang Zhu, Chunli Huang
arxiv-2601-12387.description: Abstract Chiral superconductivity is a time-reversal–symmetry-breaking superconducting phase that has attracted broad interest as a potential platform for topological quantum computation. A fundamental consequence of this symmetry breaking is orbital magnetization, yet a clear microscopic formulation of this quantity has remained elusive.

arxiv-2602-07687.title: Low-Rank Koopman Deformables with Log-Linear Time Integration Journal: TOG CCS: Computing methodologies Physical simulation
arxiv-2602-07687.creator: Yue Chang, Peter Yichen Chen, Eitan Grinspun, Maurizio M. Chiaramonte
arxiv-2602-07687.description: Abstract . We present a low-rank Koopman operator formulation for accelerating deformable subspace simulation. Using a Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) parameterization of the Koopman operator, our method learns the temporal evolution of deformable dynamics and predicts future states through efficient matrix evaluations instead of sequential time integration.

britannica-1911-tontine.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-tontine.description: Article 'Tontine' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The tontine principle has often been applied in Great Britain, at one time in connexion with government life annuities. Many such tontines were set on foot between the years 1773 and 1789, those of 1773, 1775 and 1777 being commonly called the Irish tontines, as the money was borrowed under acts of the Irish parliament. The most important English tontine was that of 1789, which was created by 29 Geo.

pmc-10522559.title: Clinical impact of screening computed tomography in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10522559.creator: Patrick D. Collins, Lorenzo Giosa, Sushil Kathar, Valentina Camarda, Filippo Palmesino, Darshan Eshwar, Nicholas A. Barrett, Andrew Retter, Francesco Vasques, Barnaby Sanderson, Sze M. Mak, Louise Rose, Luigi Camporota
pmc-10522559.description: BackgroundData on the prevalence and clinical impact of extrapulmonary findings at screening computed tomography (CT) on initiation of veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-V ECMO) are limited. We aimed to identify the prevalence of extrapulmonary findings on screening CT following V-V ECMO initiation. We hypothesized that extrapulmonary findings would influence clinical management and outcome.

pmc-11657388.title: Virtual reality simulation for facilitating critical reflection and transformative learning: pedagogical, practical, and ethical considerations
pmc-11657388.creator: Niki Soilis, Farhan Bhanji, Elizabeth Anne Kinsella
pmc-11657388.description: There is growing recognition that preparing health professionals to work with complex social issues in the delivery of healthcare requires distinct theoretical and pedagogical approaches. Recent literature highlights the significance of employing simulated environments which aim to immerse learners in the experiences of diverse populations and bridge the gap between academic learning and lived realities across a diverse society.

pmc-12381646.title: Effect of Oil Palm Leaf Meal (Elaeis guineensis) on Growth Performance, Haematology and Carcass Characteristics of West African Dwarf Sheep
pmc-12381646.creator: Paulinus Ogbonnaya Essen, Godwin Nnamdi Njoku, Godswill Uzoma Onya, Blessing Ngozi Zachary, Dondo Stephen Donkoh, Timothy Tartenger Kuka, Benjamin Adjei‐Mensah
pmc-12381646.description: BackgroundNigerian ruminant farmers face poor animal nutrition during dry seasons, affecting productivity.ObjectivesA 90‐day study evaluated the effect of oil palm leaf meal (OPLM) supplementation on the performance of West African Dwarf (WAD) weaner sheep.MethodsFifteen WAD sheep aged 4–5 months were randomly assigned to three dietary treatments in a completely randomised design.

pmc-13084443.title: Hardwood Burning as a Dominant Source of Fine Particulate Matter from Biomass Burning in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
pmc-13084443.creator: Ngoc Tran, Yusuke Fujii, To Thi Hien, Norimichi Takenaka
pmc-13084443.description: While biomass burning (BB) significantly affects air quality in Southeast Asia, its contribution to PM2.5 in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC), Vietnam’s most populous city, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify the major BB sources contributing to PM2.

pmc-13455373.title: Bacillus inoculation drives fine-scale taxonomic shifts in the bacterial communities of saline–alkaline wheat rhizosphere soil
pmc-13455373.creator: Huicheng Zhao, Linqi Zhang, Mengshuai Liu, Xinhui Fu, Meiyu Liu, Peng Guo, Wenliang Yang
pmc-13455373.description: BackgroundSoil salinization severely restricts wheat production in the coastal regions of northern China, and inoculation with plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) is a promising strategy for alleviating salt stress. However, the response mechanisms of indigenous bacterial communities to PGPR remain unclear, partly because of the limitations of short-read sequencing in terms of taxonomic resolution.
